# Claims register (generated by `g4bench claims` from configs/claims.yaml)

Status is computed only from measured results in `results/` (exact hardware, baseline configs). Measured comparison rows available: 750.

| id | claim | kind | status |
|---|---|---|---|
| C01 | vLLM 0.33.0 (MTP 4 tokens, async scheduling, gpu-mem 0.90, prefix caching off) output throughput on 1x RTX PRO 6000, Gemma 4 12B BF16, at ISL {1K,8K} x conc {1,4,16,64}, OSL 1K | measurable | measured 8/8 (8 consistent) |
| C02 | SGLang 0.5.23 (NEXTN 5 steps / 6 draft tokens, mem 0.85, radix cache off) output throughput at the same 8 workloads | measurable | measured 8/8 (8 higher) - descriptive, n<3 |
| C03 | Open-engine latency figures: p99 TPOT, p99 E2EL and p90 TTFT for vLLM and SGLang at the 8 workloads | measurable | measured 48/48 (25 consistent, 7 higher, 16 lower) - descriptive, n<3 |
| C04 | vLLM outperforms SGLang by 1.4-2.1x in throughput/TPOT at every workload (implied by the article's ratio tables; Backboard cancels out) | measurable | measured 8/8: vLLM/SGLang 1.31-1.84x (article 1.42-2.08x) - descriptive, n<3 |
| C05 | Backboard's engine achieves the reported throughput/latency and wins 208/208 metric comparisons | untestable | untestable (see reason) |
| C06 | Backboard's draft head shortlists candidates in 4-bit and rescores in BF16 without changing the BF16 target output | untestable | untestable (see reason) |
| C07 | The competitor flags stated in the article match the engines' published recipes (and exist at the pinned versions) | verified-source | verified (sources) |

## Notes

- **C01**: E2: all 8 workloads at seed 0 (n=1; 8192x4 n=2), +0.9 to +3.1 % vs the article. The same recipe is side A of the same-GPU pairs (results/pairs/): 6-10 runs per workload, +0.5 to +1.6 % vs the article; the status uses that larger set
- **C02**: E3: all 8 workloads at seed 0 (n=1), +6.8 to +16.5 % vs the article; SGLang auto-caps at 48 running requests, so its c64 points queue
- **C03**: measured by the same runs as C01/C02
- **C04**: seed-matched comparison of the E2/E3 runs (g4bench analyze -> engine_comparison.csv), n=1 per workload
- **C05**: Backboard's engine, kernels and raw data are proprietary/unpublished; only its reported numbers exist. We can at most bound them against open-engine results on the same workload.
- **C06**: Implementation unavailable. The open analogue built here is an FP8 draft-head scan with exact BF16 rescoring of the top 32 candidates (image patch mtp_draft_head_q, D-054, admissibility b), part of the final config.
- **C07**: Engine flags match vllm-project/recipes gemma-4-12B-it.yaml (fa1173a1) and the SGLang Gemma4 cookbook; every flag exists at the pinned tags (configs/engine_flags/, D-023). Unstated defaults (max-model-len, scheduler limits, attention backend) are recorded per run from server logs (D-025).
- **C08**: 16/24 published (p99 E2EL, p99 TPOT) pairs are impossible with fixed 1024-token outputs (src/g4bench/inference_checks.py), consistent with InferenceX RANDOM_RANGE_RATIO=0.8 (D-004).
- **C09**: Every run records nvidia-smi name, power limits, clocks, driver; exact_hardware flag. E1 (2026-11-11): Modal's GPU is the RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition, 600 W power limit, driver 610.57.04; the article does not state its edition, so equality cannot be checked.
- **C10**: Stated in the article's limitations; our design labels n<3 results descriptive and reports same-GPU paired ratios with t-CIs over pairs (D-005, D-061).
- **C11**: Not stated in the article. We pin InferenceX 0b991451 and range ratio 0.8 (the InferenceX default), fingerprint the resulting request streams for seeds 0-2, and report the choice as an assumption.
